title: Becanus: no venial is properly against the law’s end; all are somehow against law
source_text: XXIX. Quibus consentanea tradit Becanus Jesuita in Summa Theologiae Scholasticae, tomo secundo, tractatu secundo, capite secundo, quaestione septima, ubi haec est ejus prima conclusio, Nullum peccatum veniale est proprie contra finem legis. Secunda vero haec, Tametsi nullum peccatum veniale sit contra finem legis, omne tamen veniale est aliquo modo contra legem, sive perfecte, sive imperfecte.
pass_a_gloss: Things agreeing with these Becanus the Jesuit hands down in the Summa of Scholastic Theology, second volume, second treatise, second chapter, seventh question, where this is his first conclusion: No venial sin is properly against the end of the law. But the second is this: Although no venial sin is against the end of the law, yet every venial is in some way against the law, whether perfectly or imperfectly.
pass_b_english: Becanus: venial sin is never properly against the law’s end (charity).
Yet every venial is somehow against the law—perfectly or imperfectly.
